memory_candidates.content: Portable, ecosystem-general shell one-liners to read a package's declared version without a language runtime, verified sandbox-safe (sed/grep/jq only, no GNU-awk 3-arg match()): pyproject.toml (PEP 621) -- `sed -n '/^\[project\]/,/^\[/p' f | grep -m1 '^version[[:space:]]*=' | sed -E 's/^version[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*"([^"]*)".*/\1/'` (section-scoped so a later [tool.poetry] table never false-matches); setup.cfg [metadata] with the same pattern minus quotes; setup.py via a best-effort literal-kwarg grep (correctly yields empty, not a false positive, for programmatic versions); package.json via `jq -r '.version // empty'`; Cargo.toml [package] with the pyproject-style pattern (correctly yields empty for `version.workspace = true`, since the `.` breaks the anchor). All five fall through to empty (not a false match) for the 'version not statically declared here' cases (PEP 621 dynamic, Cargo workspace inheritance) -- treat that as an honest signal, not a bug to work around.

When a skill/command markdown file documents a shell step's expected output as an 'Error Handling' transcript, verify the transcript by diffing it token-by-token against the actual `echo` string literals in that step's code block -- do not write the transcript from a design doc's suggested wording and assume it matches. A transcript documenting a message the code does not actually emit is worse than no transcript, because it looks authoritative. When multiple discovered items (not just one) can appear in a mismatch report, an inline single-value 'Error: X does not match Y' line does not generalize -- move the enumerable facts to a separate labeled list below the Error line instead of forcing them into one interpolated sentence.

To end-to-end test a new shell step embedded in a skill's markdown documentation before trusting it, extract the step's code block verbatim by line-range (sed -n '<start>,<end>p') directly from the source-store .md file -- not a hand-retyped copy -- and assemble it with the preceding steps' variable-setup blocks (also extracted verbatim) into a runnable harness script. This proves the *actual documented code* works, including its interaction with sibling steps' variables, rather than testing a paraphrase that could silently diverge from what ships.
